blocks.explanation:
Algebraic times trigonometric, like Example 29.
Plan: \(x\) first (it becomes 1), \(\cos 2x\) second, one integration by parts.
steps:
Given: \(\int x\cos 2x\,dx\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: integration by parts with \(f(x) = x\), \(g(x) = \cos 2x\).

Apply integration by parts
\[= x\cdot\dfrac{\sin 2x}{2} - \int \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\cdot 1\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \sin 2x\,dx\]
Why: \(\int \cos 2x\,dx = \frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) (divide by 2 because of the chain rule); \(\frac{d}{dx}x = 1\).

Integrate \(\sin 2x\)
\[= \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\cos 2x}{2}\right) + c\]
\[= \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4} + c\]
Why: \(\int \sin 2x\,dx = -\frac{\cos 2x}{2}\); minus times minus is plus.

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2} + x\cos 2x - \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\]
\[= x\cos 2x\]
Why: the \(\frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) terms cancel.
